author: Jeremy Goldstein
title: OG Anunoby injury fears after Knicks star asked to leave game in NBA Playoffs - NewsBreak
text:
By Jeremy Goldstein ,
52 minutes ago The New York Knicks won a fifth consecutive NBA playoff game on Wednesday, holding on to knock off a Joel Embiid-less Philadelphia 76ers team 108-102 at Madison Square Garden.
Besides a Jalen Brunson shooting slump and Spike Lee missing the game to attend a sporting event elsewhere , everything went right for the Knicks until 3:08 left in the fourth quarter.
Forward OG Anunoby, arguably New York's best player throughout the playoffs, took himself out of the game after appearing to pull his hamstring on a non-contact play while running through the lane on an offensive possession. On the same play, Anunoby received the pass and went up for the dunk, but was blocked by Paul George. His injury came after OKC Thunder's bench was left turning away in disgust after a gruesome Lakers injury the previous night.

• First female trainer to win Kentucky Derby immediately loses thousands of prize money
Anunoby started limping back on defense before taking himself out of the game. He finished with 24 points on 9-17 shooting in 37 minutes, his fourth 20-point game of the playoffs.
Knicks coach Mike Brown wasn't quite sure what happened. "I haven't talked to anybody. He looked like he was hopping. I have not talked to medical yet," he said at his post-game presser.
Brunson, who finished with 26 points on 9-21 shooting in 41 minutes, also didn't know what happened and tried to downplay considering it a serious injury. “I’ll cross that bridge when we get to it. I don’t know too much," he told reporters.
Insider Kris Pursianen added more smoke with his social media report. "Reporters coming back from the Knicks' locker room are saying OG Anunoby wasn't in there, and players wouldn't really speak about his health, understandably," he tweeted.
The Knicks traded homegrown draft picks RJ Barrett, Immanuel Quickley, and draft capital to the Toronto Raptors for Anunboy — the big, two-way wing the team was missing — midway through the 2023/24 NBA season.
He was hurt in the team's run to the second round of the 2024 playoffs but played a big part in helping New York reach the Eastern Conference Finals in 2025 for the first time in a generation.

• OKC Thunder players look away in disgust after gruesome Lakers injury
Philadelphia will look to rebound at home in Game 3. 76ers rookie VJ Edgecombe, the third pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, seemed optimistic.
"We're not going to give up," he said post-game. "They did what they had to do and protect home court. We won't give up. We're going to keep playing hard regardless."
Edgecombe thought the 76ers could have won Game 2. "We felt like we should've won it," he said. "It came down to shot-making at the end of the game. They were making shots, we wasn't."
